grammar.title: Narrative tenses
grammar.shortAr: نستخدم الماضي البسيط والمستمر والتام لسرد القصص وترتيب الأحداث.
points: Past simple: main completed events in a story
Past continuous: background information and temporary past situations
Past perfect: an action that happened before the main events
table: Suddenly, he heard a terrible crash.
Josh was walking down the road when he heard the crash.
The sun was shining. The wind was blowing.
When we arrived at the station, the train had already left.
I realised I had left my phone in the car.

lessons.title: Less is more?
goals: Use verb patterns after verbs and prepositions
Distinguish 'go on doing' from 'go on to do'

grammar.title: Verb patterns
grammar.shortAr: بعد حروف الجر نستخدم غالبًا -ing، وبعض الأفعال يغيّر معناها مع المصدر.
points: After a preposition (except to), the second verb is usually -ing
Phrasal verbs are usually followed by an -ing form
Some verbs change meaning with to + infinitive or -ing: stop, remember, go on, grow up
table: You should think about doing that course.
I look forward to reading your new book!
She went on dancing even after her accident.
She went on to be a great dancer.
I stopped to talk to Felipe.
exceptions: Look forward to takes -ing because to is a preposition here.

lessons.title: Don't forget to …

grammar.title: How to … leave phone messages
grammar.shortAr: للطلب المباشر: Can/Could you...؟ ولغير المباشر: I wonder if you could...
points: Direct requests: Can/Could you ...?, Will/Would you ... please?
Indirect requests soften the request: Do you think you could ...?, I wonder if you'd mind ...-ing
In indirect requests, word order stays like an affirmative statement
table: Would you look for it, please?
Do you think you could have a look for it for me?
I wonder if you'd mind helping me lock up.
It's Max here. / This is Max speaking.
exceptions: On the phone say 'It's Max here' or 'This is Max speaking', NOT 'I'm Max'.

lessons.title: Your gadgets
goals: Use except for, apart from and (not) even
Talk about gadgets and screen time

grammar.title: except for, apart from, (not) even
grammar.shortAr: except for / apart from تعني «باستثناء»، وeven للتأكيد على المفاجأة.
points: except for + noun says one thing is not included
apart from + noun means the same as except for
even emphasises something surprising; not even emphasises a surprising negative
table: The school teaches most ball sports except for golf.
All the children are here except for Leila.
We're open every day apart from Sunday.
John doesn't usually watch TV, but even he liked that programme!
Not even Jo, whose English is very good, could understand him.
exceptions: Use except that before a clause; use except (for) before a noun.

vocab.example: I could live without all my gadgets apart from my phone.
I'd say my smartwatch is one gadget I could live without.
My laptop is pretty important for work.
I love a range of gadgets from my Xbox and my laptop.
Guitar pedals change the way my guitar sounds.
People spend too much time on their screens.
They'd posted photos on social media.

practice.why: The phone is the one thing not included.
